subject: Escalation request: Silverline open-book pricing + SLA ask (renewal)
messages:
From: Elena Rojas <elena.rojas@silverline.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.io
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 14:10:00 -0400
Subject: Renewal discussion: pricing & SLA after incident

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As we discussed, Silverline is preparing our renewal and we need to resolve two items before legal will approve:

1) Credits for the October availability incident (we tracked ~18 hours degraded throughput across our prod clusters) — we are looking for a one-time make-good to offset the outage impact on our Q4 projects.
2) Contract term/commit flexibility — given our growth profile we're asking to move to a more flexible 24-month term with a true-up cadence, not the rigid 36-month commit in the current quote.

We'd also like an SLA addendum guaranteeing a 99.9% monthly availability target for the first 12 months of the renewal with a modest service credit schedule. Without these items the procurement and legal teams will hold the renewal.

Can you share what concessions Redwood can offer? We are aiming to sign in early November if terms are acceptable.

Attachments: Silverline_Incident_Summary_20261015.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Elena
Director of Platform Engineering
Silverline Analytics
From: priyom_das@redwood.io
To: Elena Rojas <elena.rojas@silverline.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.io, rishi_malhotra@redwood.io
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:24:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: pricing & SLA after incident

Elena —

Appreciate the clear summary and the incident write-up. I spoke with CS and finance this morning; below is the proposal we think will get us to an executable renewal while balancing economics:

- One-time operational credit: $48,000 applied at execution (to address incident impact).
- Renewal discount: 20% off list for the contracted commit in year 1, with standard volume tiers thereafter.
- Term: propose a 24-month renewed term (resets the commit basis), with a mid-term true-up review at month 12.
- SLA addendum: 99.9% monthly availability guaranteed for the first 12 months. If we miss SLA the credit schedule will be 5%/10%/20% depending on severity.

I've attached a draft renewal quote that reflects these numbers. This package requires exec sign-off for the credit and non-standard term reset — I am escalating to Marissa and Vivek.

Proposed next step: if you confirm the above as acceptable, I'll circulate a signed addendum + updated quote for legal to start paperwork.

Attachments: Draft_Renewal_Quote_DL-8471.xlsx

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: priyom_das@redwood.io
To: marissa_cole@redwood.io, rishi_malhotra@redwood.io, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.io
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 09:00:00 -04:00
Subject: Escalation: Silverline renewal — exec approval required for concession bundle

Team,

Looping you in for fast approval. Silverline (DL-8471) is a strategic account with rising consumption (+45% YoY in Q3). They signalled a hard deadline from procurement: legal will not execute without a one-time credit and an SLA addendum. If we don't realign terms we risk them pausing the renewal and testing alternatives.

Summary of ask (customer expectation):
- One-time credit: $48k
- Renewal discount: 20% list (Customer expects us to be aggressive given the outage)
- Term: reset to 24 months with a 12-month true-up review
- SLA addendum: 99.9% monthly availability for 12 months with outlined credits

Economic impact (high level):
- ARR at risk ~ $620k annualized; concession bundle reduces NPV by ~ $75k on conservative model (attached).
- Upside: customer has signaled willingness to increase committed usage if performance is stable — potential +35% ARR growth over 12 months.

Attachments: Concession_Economics_DL-8471.csv

Ask: Exec approval for the above concession bundle or counter guidance (max discount, credit cap, term constraints). If approved, I will ask Legal to prepare the SLA addendum and Finance to process the credit. Time-sensitive: customer expects signoff by 10/29 to hit procurement window.

Thanks,
Priyom
From: marissa_cole@redwood.io
To: priyom_das@redwood.io, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.io
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.io
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 11:35:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: Silverline renewal — exec approval required for concession bundle

Priyom / Vivek —

I support a concession to retain Silverline but recommend tighter guardrails:
- Approve up to 25% discount contingent on a mutual-growth clause (customer commits to +30% minimum ARR growth vs baseline in 12 months).
- One-time credit: approve up to $50k but require Finance sign-off on timing and revenue recognition impact.
- SLA addendum: approve 99.9% for 12 months, but Legal must insert a rollback clause that reverts to standard SLA if customer does not meet the mutual-growth milestones.

If Finance and Legal can operationalize the above quickly, I ok the escalation. Priyom — please secure the customer commitment in writing and push legal to draft the addendum.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, North America Sales

Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.io, legal@redwood.io
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 16:07:00 -04:00
Subject: Final: Silverline concession approval (conditional)

Team —

After reviewing the economics and Marissa's recommendations, I approve a conditional concession package for Silverline:

- Discount: 22% off year-1 list price (compromise between 20/25).
- One-time operational credit: $40,000 applied at execution.
- Term: 24 months with a mandatory true-up review at month 12.
- SLA: 99.9% monthly availability for 12 months. Legal to include a rollback clause tied to the mutual-growth milestone and a cap on cumulative credits.

Conditions:
1) Sales (Priyom) to secure the customer's signed commitment to the mutual-growth clause before Legal issues the addendum.
2) Finance to confirm revenue recognition treatment for the credit and confirm no material impact to Q4 forecasts.
3) Legal to draft the SLA addendum with the rollback language and cap on credits.

Priyom — proceed to obtain the signed commitment and loop Legal/Finance. I'll be available if there are final questions before the procurement deadline.

-Vivek
